items.stem: What is happening whenever you hear a sound?

options.rationale: Correct: all sounds come from vibrating objects.
Temperature change does not make the sound.
Sound always comes from a vibration, which is movement.

items.explanation: Correct: all sounds come from vibrating objects.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO changes would make a plucked rubber band sound HIGHER in pitch? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: a shorter band vibrates faster, giving a higher pitch.
Correct: a tighter band vibrates faster, raising the pitch.
Plucking gently changes loudness, not pitch.
A longer band vibrates slower, giving a lower pitch.

items.explanation: Correct: a shorter band vibrates faster, giving a higher pitch.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Why does a voice sound quieter the further away the person is?

options.text: The sound spreads out and loses energy as it travels
options.rationale: Correct: sound energy spreads and weakens with distance.

options.text: The person is vibrating less far away
options.rationale: Their vibration is the same; the sound just spreads out.

options.text: Sound cannot travel more than a few steps
options.rationale: Sound travels far, just getting quieter.

options.text: Distance changes the pitch to silence
options.rationale: Distance affects loudness, not pitch to silence.

items.explanation: Correct: sound energy spreads and weakens with distance.
